Honourable Smt.Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3705 Of 2009
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the dismissal order dated 26.06.2007 (hereinafter will be referred as 'impugned order') passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal - cum - I Additional District Judge,
Mahabubnagar (hereinafter will be referred as 'Tribunal") in O.P.No.364 of 2005, the petitioner/claimant has filed the present Appeal to set aside the order and seeks just and reasonable compensation.

entities.text:
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal - cum - I Additional District Judge,
Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case as can be seen from the record are that the petitioner has filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.1,50,000/-
from the respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3 for the death of deceased by name "Velgonda Nagaiah"
(hereinafter will be referred as 'deceased').
Petitioner No.1 is the nephew/adopted son of the deceased.

The reason assigned by the petitioner for the death of the deceased is that on 17.01.2005 at about 1:00 midnight hours, while the deceased was returning home after MGP,J attending to calls of nature in the outskirts of the village, the driver of the APSRTC Bus bearing registration No. AP 22 U 8646, (for brevity hereinafter called as "crime vehicle") drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner in reverse direction and dashed the deceased.
Due to the said accident, the deceased fell down and sustained multiple injuries all over his body.
Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Mahabubnagar in the same crime vehicle for treatment where, he succumbed to the injuries on 28.01.2005.

Based on the complaint Police, Jadcherla registered case in FIR No.21/2005 under Section 337 of Indian Penal Code, 1806 against driver of the crime vehicle and later altered the Section of law to Section 304-A of Indian Penal Code, 1806, after investigation filed charge sheet.
4.
According to the claim petitioner, the deceased was aged about 70 years at the time of accident and was earning Rs.100/-per day as coolie.
It was further stated that the petitioner is adopted son of the deceased.
Due to the sudden demise of the deceased in the said accident, the family suffered a lot and lost love and affection of the deceased.

Therefore, the petitioner filed petition seeking compensation of Rs.1,50,000/-
MGP,J (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand) against respondents jointly and severally.

5. The respondent No.1, who is the owner of the hired crime vehicle (APSRTC Bus) remained exparte and whereas, the respondent No.2 Insurance company filed counter denying all the averments in the claim petition including age, avocation, income, manner of accident apart from denying its liability.

It also contended that the accident occurred due to self negligence on part of the A.Chennaiah vs V.S.R.K. Rasad And 2 Others on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50834632/
1 deceased.

entities.text: A.Chennaiah vs V.S.R.K. Rasad And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was specifically contended that the alleged crime vehicle was hired to APSRTC, as such,
APSRTC alone is liable to satisfy the compensation payable.
On the above grounds prayed to dismiss the claim application.

6. The respondent No.3, Andhra Pradesh Road Transportation Corporation filed counter denying the manner of accident as narrated in the claim application, rather the accident occurred due to the self negligence of the deceased.
It was further stated that neither the alleged crime vehicle nor the driver was under the control or supervision of the Corporation.
The owner and insurer of the same are liable to pay compensation if awarded by this court.
On these grounds, the respondent No.3 prayed to dismiss the claim petition against it.
MGP,J 7.
Based on the rival contentions, the Tribunal has framed the following three issues.

i) Whether the accident occurred on 17.01.2005, at about at 1:00am at Gollapally bus stand, due to rash and negligent driving of offending bus bearing No. AP.22.U.8646 by its driver and whether it resulted in causing death of the deceased V.Nagaiah?
ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation?

If so, to what amount,
and from whom?
ii) To what relief?
8.
During the course of trial, PWs 1 and 2 were examined and got marked Exs.A1 to A7.
On behalf of respondent No.3, its representative was examined as RW1, however, no documents were marked.
The learned Tribunal after considering the rival contentions dismissed the claim petition.
Aggrieved by the impugned order, the appellant/petitioners preferred the present Appeal to set aside the impugned order and grant just and reasonable compensation.

9. Heard both sides and perused the record including the grounds of Appeal.
10.
The first and foremost contention of the petitioner is that the learned Tribunal erred in declaring that the driver of the bus was not at rash and negligence in causing the accident.
MGP,J 11.
The sole petitioner, who was examined as PW1, categorically deposed about the manner of the accident, however, he is not an eyewitness to the accident.

The petitioner got examined one K.
Rangaiah as PW2 to establish the manner of accident.
PW2 deposed that on 17.01.2005 at 1.00 AM RTC bus bearing No. AP 22 U 8646 came to their village.

PW2 further deposed that he along with other neighbouring owners went near the bus stand to enquire as to why the bus came in the midnight and in the meanwhile the driver of the bus took the bus in reverse direction at high speed in rash and negligent manner, without noticing the persons coming on the back side of the bus and

A.Chennaiah vs V.S.R.K. Rasad And 2 Others on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50834632/
2 dashed against the deceased Velgonda Nagaiah, who was returning home after attending calls of nature in the outskirts of Gollapalli Village.

entities.text: A.Chennaiah vs V.S.R.K. Rasad And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the course of cross examination, a suggestion was given to PW2 by the learned counsel for the respondent that despite of hearing the noise of the engine of the bus, the deceased negligently crossed the road and that the driver was not negligent.
PW2 denied the said suggestion.

A duty is cast on the driver of the bus to look at the back side of the bus through convex mirror/rear view mirror while reversing the bus so as to ascertain whether anybody is there at the back side.
It is not the case of the respondent that MGP,J despite blowing horn the deceased has crossed the bus.
Nothing is elicited in the cross examination of PW2 to establish that he has not witnessed the accident.
That apart the petitioner has also relied upon the documentary evidence under Exs.A1 to A3 i.e., certified copies of FIR, inquest report and MVI report.
A perusal of these documents discloses that an accident occurred on 17.01.2005.

Further,
Exs.A1 and A2 discloses that in the said accident a person by name Velgonda Nagaiah died.

12. The learned Tribunal observed in the impugned order that the petitioner has not examined the driver of conductor of the offending bus to explain their conduct subsequent to the accident and that their evidence would have also become useful to test the veracity of the evidence of PW2 about the presence of eyewitness to the accident at the scene of offence.

13. It is pertinent to place reliance on the decision of Honorable Apex Court in Anita Sharma and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited and another 1 wherein it was observed that standards of proof like in a criminal trial are inapplicable in Motor Accident Claims cases and standards to be followed in such claims is one based on preponderance of 1 2021 (1) SCC 171 MGP,J probability rather than establishing the case beyond reasonable doubt, as the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 itself is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the prime objective of providing relief to the family members, who lost their family member in a vehicular accident.

entities.text: Anita Sharma and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited and another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Unfortunately in the present case the learned Tribunal erred in adjudicating the matter like a criminal trial,
discarding the evidence on record and the version of eyewitness to the incident.

Moreover, until and unless there is prima facie material to establish that the crime vehicle was involved in the alleged accident, the police would not have registered the case against the driver of the crime vehicle.

In Kusum Lata and others v. Satbir & others 2, the Honourable Supreme Court observed as under:
"It is well known that in a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be done in a criminal trial.

entities.text: Kusum Lata and others v. Satbir & others 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Court must keep this distinction in mind."
14.

The observation of the learned Tribunal in the impugned order that since no complaint has been lodged for five days after the accident, the circumstance throws doubt on the probability of accident being witnessed by the an eyewitness.

It is significant to bear in mind that after the accident happens and intimation about the accident is received by the family members 2 2011 (3) SCC 646 MGP,J of the deceased, their primary concern is to take care of the injured in his critical condition.

The health and well-being of the injured is their priority rather than to lodge an FIR and it cannot be expected that close relatives of the injured or deceased person would rush to police station immediately to lodge complaint rather than taking steps to provide immediate treatment.

Moreover,
in Ex.A1 FIR it was categorically mentioned that as the de-facto complainant (petitioner) was not A.Chennaiah vs V.S.R.K. Rasad And 2 Others on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50834632/
3 available in the village, he could not lodge complaint immediately after the accident.

entities.text: A.Chennaiah vs V.S.R.K. Rasad And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the deceased was admitted in the hospital and while undergoing treatment he succumbed to injuries after five days of the incident.
It is settled law that, when the valid and sufficient reasons are explained, the delay in lodging complaint cannot be considered as fatal.
Thus, delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case.

15. The learned Tribunal observed in the impugned order that non filing of charge sheet by the police also strengthens conclusion that the investigating officer was also not satisfied with the allegation that the accident occurred due to negligent of the driver of the RTC Bus.
It is to be seen that the petitioner relied upon Ex.A7 i.e., returned copy application No.22/2007 MGP,J dated 08.01.2007 of JFCM, Jadcherla.

A perusal of Ex.A7 disclose that when the petitioner applied for certified copies of charge sheet, postmortem examination report and motor vehicle inspector report but the same was returned on the ground that the said documents were not received by the Court.
Thus, it is clear that the claimant has made his efforts to secure charge sheet but he could not file the same as the said charge sheet was not received by the court.
At this stage reference can be made to a decision of Honourable Apex Court in the case of Sunita and Others.
v. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Others 3, wherein it was observed as under:

"It is thus well settled that in motor accident claim cases, once the foundational fact,
namely, the actual occurrence of the accident, has been established, then the Tribunal's role would be to calculate the quantum of just compensation if the accident had taken place by reason of negligence of the driver of a motor vehicle and,
while doing so, the Tribunal would not be strictly bound by the pleadings of the parties.

Notably, while deciding cases arising out of motor vehicle accidents, the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases."

16. In view of the principle laid down in the above said decision it is clear that in motor accident claim cases the crucial 3 2020 (13) SCC 486 MGP,J aspect is with regard to actual occurrence of the accident.

While a charge sheet can indicate potential negligence, it is not considered as conclusive proof on its own and should be evaluated alongside other evidence like eyewitness testimonies and other official records.

17. In view of the above discussion and also considering the principle laid down in the above said decisions and also in view of the oral evidence of PWs 1 and 2 coupled with documentary evidence under Exs.A1 to A3, this court is of considered view that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle by its driver.

18. The other contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the learned Tribunal erred in disallowing the petition without relying on the evidence of the petitioner, who categorically deposed on oath that he was the adopted son and dependent.

4 19.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of page No.7 and paragraph No.17 of the impugned order, it makes it clear that the learned Tribunal while answering issue No.2 observed that the petitioner cannot be held as dependent of the deceased as the version of PW1 that he was adopted by the deceased 10 years back is not proved by MGP,J any legal evidence.

In Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation v.
Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai 4 the Honourable Supreme Court opined that an application made by the nephew of the deceased, who died on account of a motor vehicle accident was clearly maintainable.

entities.text:
Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation v.
Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. Now coming to the quantum of compensation, the learned Tribunal fixed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per annum and deducted 50% towards personal expenses.
The learned Tribunal applied '5' as multiplier as per II Schedule to Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicle Act.
The learned Tribunal awarded Rs.5,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.3,000/- towards hospital expenses.

Accordingly, the learned Tribunal calculated Rs.35,000/- as compensation, however, did not award any amount on the ground that the petitioner failed to establish that the petitioner failed to establish that he is the dependent of the deceased.
21. It is to be seen that the claim petition was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act but not under Section 163- 4 1987 AIR 1690 MGP,J A of the Motor Vehicle Act.
Moreover, the learned Tribunal has framed an issue with regard to establishing rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle by its driver.

Once a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal frames an issue regarding the establishment of "rash and negligent driving" by the driver of the vehicle involved in an accident, the petition is considered to be filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, which allows a person to claim compensation arising from a motor vehicle accident by proving the fault or negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thus, the learned Tribunal ought not to have fixed the notional income and multiplier as per II schedule to 163-A of the Motor Vehicle Act.
22. As per the averments of the claim petition, the age of the deceased is claimed to be 70 years as on the date of the accident.
No documentary evidence is adduced on behalf of the petitioner to establish the age of the deceased.
However, in Ex.A1 FIR, the age of the deceased was mentioned as 55 years.
However, in inquest report under Ex.A2, the age of the deceased was mentioned as 75 years.

Thus,
this Court is inclined to consider the age of the deceased as 75 years.

The appropriate multiplier for the persons, who are aged more than 65 years MGP,J would be "5", as per the decision of the Apex Court in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 5.
23.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now coming to the income of the deceased, the learned Tribunal by considering the age of the deceased fixed the notional income at Rs.10,000/- per annum.
The claimant alleged in the claim petition that the deceased was earning Rs.2,500/- per month as a coolie, however, no document is filed to establish the same.
As per Exs.A1 and A2, the deceased was shown as coolie.
Considering the age of the deceased and the standard of living of a coolie in the year 2005, this Court is inclined to consider the age of the deceased at Rs.2,250/- per month i.e., Rs.75/- per day.
Since the deceased is not having any other family members except the petitioner, 50% of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.1,125/- per month.

A.Chennaiah vs V.S.R.K. Rasad And 2 Others on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50834632/
5 24.

entities.text: A.Chennaiah vs V.S.R.K. Rasad And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.13,500/- (Rs.1,125/- x 12 months).
Since the deceased is more than 65 years, the question of considering future prospects does not arise.

When the annual income of the deceased after deducting 5 2009 ACJ 1298 (SC) MGP,J personal expenses is multiplied with relevant multiplier i.e., '5', the loss of dependency would be Rs.67,500/-
(Rs.13,500/- x 5).
In addition thereto, under the conventional heads, the claimant is awarded Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.3,000/- towards medical expenses.

Thus, in all the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,00,500/-.
25.
Now coming to the liability, there is no dispute that the crime vehicle belongs to respondent No.1 and the same was insured with respondent No.2.
However, the crime vehicle was hired with respondent No.3 APSRTC Corporation.

The learned Tribunal while relying on the decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation v. Kailash Nath Kothari 6, wherein it was held that when an RTC hires a private bus and it is involved in an accident, the RTC can be held liable as the principal employer of the driver.

entities.text: Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation v. Kailash Nath Kothari 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is clear that when a vehicle is hired by an RTC and is involved in an accident, the RTC, being in control of the vehicle, is primarily liable.

6 (1997) 7 SCC 481 MGP,J 26. In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the considered view that the learned Tribunal erred in dismissing the claim petition, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.
27. In the result, the Appeal is allowed by setting aside the passed by the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal - cum - I Additional District Judge, Mahabubnagar in O.P.No.364 of 2005.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal - cum - I Additional District Judge, Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the claim petition filed by the petitioner in M.V.O.P.No.364 of 2005 is allowed in part by awarding compensation of Rs.1,00,500/-, which shall carry interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the claim application till the date of realization.
The respondent No.3 is liable to deposit the compensation amount within one month from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw entire compensation awarded to him without furnishing any security.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
